question: Red (carneous) degeneration of a fibroid occurs most commonly during pregnancy due to venous thrombosis and haemorrhage within the fibroid, and it is managed conservatively with analgesics.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Red degeneration is a pregnancy-associated complication caused by venous thrombosis within the fibroid. It presents with localised tenderness and fever, and is managed conservatively. Surgery is NOT indicated acutely.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Red degeneration (carneous degeneration) occurs characteristically in pregnancy, caused by infarction from venous outflow obstruction. Treatment is conservative — analgesics, hydration — and surgery is avoided during pregnancy.
